review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner (self-review, not independent approval)
review.decision: Reconcile only an exact historical frontend observation with a completed turn and positively gone frontend; preserve new work and unknown ownership
review.notes: Observed defect: a late ID-less Resumed is newer than its task_complete, leaving working in the native store after the exact managed frontend has exited. A live shared backend alone is not a new external client. Use the existing frontend binding receipt and exact full observation generation, home/thread/backend incarnation, bound-time ordering, ESRCH for its frontend PID, then re-read receipt and observation so a concurrent new binding/update defeats the proof. Never delete the observation, change consent or use title/cwd/PID alone as ownership. Radar reconciles only working Resumed with a latest non-ambiguous past completed/aborted boundary, no conflicting explicit turn ID, and independently verified shared backend role. Per-gather backend-role memoization is shared with the existing completed-history filter. Fresh submit/start/wait, changed same-second generation, no/mismatched binding, live/unknown frontend, legacy nonshared process, different home, new task_started and ambiguous/future evidence retain existing visibility. Explicit HQ follow retains an idle history row. No hook rearming, reap mechanism, real state mutation, installed runtime update or authority changes. Kernel/process and store seams are exercised independently; actual assembled radar tests use an isolated HOME, real exited child and actual persisted binding/rollout. Tests are not real-device/UI acceptance. Old exact radar assembly/status code must fail the new closed-worker visibility case; preserve negative controls and restore source bytes. The normal newer-completion path also consumes the same typed lifecycle fact and rejects future or ambiguous facts; otherwise that path could preempt the new conservative preservation controls. This is a bounded safety correction, not a new ownership heuristic. Follow-up owner review: ESRCH-only proof would lose its historical conclusion when an unrelated process later reuses the old frontend PID. Also accept a current process born strictly after binding publication plus the existing 120-second ps tolerance, only after a successful live PID probe and a known nonfuture start. Unknown/EPERM, old or tolerance-overlapping starts retain visibility. Add an independently mapped case before this follow-up implementation; existing HXF-001/HXF-002 case objects remain unchanged.

cases.description: Exact closed frontend observation proof is read-only, identity scoped and race conservative
cases.setup: Isolated native store, actual Save/ConfirmBinding receipts and controlled frontend PID probe; original/new observation and receipt generations
cases.action: Probe original snapshot under ESRCH, alive, EPERM, missing/corrupt receipt, wrong home/thread/backend, wrong era, then replace record or binding during the probe
cases.expected: Only the exact original backend observation tied to a positively gone verified frontend matches; every incomplete/changed/unknown case returns false; later generation wins even within one second; no observation, history or binding is removed or rewritten

cases.description: Actual radar excludes a completed managed worker revived only by a late Resumed while retaining genuine external work
cases.setup: Actual nativePanes assembly with isolated native Save/ConfirmBinding and Codex rollout metadata, exact real process birth, real exited frontend child, controlled shared-backend role and explicit follow
cases.action: Render completed and aborted old workers after late Resumed, then vary explicit turn ID, newer observation/start/submit/wait, live frontend, unknown/mismatched proof, backend role, future/ambiguous boundary and explicit follow; inspect persistent record and output JSON
cases.expected: Only completed exact closed-backend observations become idle/history; unfollowed history is absent, explicit follow remains idle and status-only without new input/read/knowledge authority. New starts/submits/waits, different turns/homes, changed generations and uncertain evidence remain visible with their existing states. Observation/history/consent bytes persist unchanged; backend role is evaluated once per process in a gather. The exact old radar code fails the new historical-worker visibility assertion while preservation controls pass

cases.description: A reused frontend PID cannot revive the old bound observation
cases.setup: Isolated actual native record/binding and controlled PID/start probes; binding published well before the current time
cases.action: Vary ESRCH, live original incarnation, known replacement born beyond the binding tolerance, unknown/EPERM, within-tolerance and future starts; replace the observation during the birth read
cases.expected: ESRCH or a positively later nonfuture process birth proves only the old frontend is gone; every unknown/original/overlapping/future case remains conservative, and a newly written observation wins; no native state is deleted or rewritten. The previous ESRCH-only implementation fails the replacement-incarnation case
